emerging_technology: Item-level passive UHF RFID in apparel retail
intended_application: Weekly shadow cycle count for one denim category at one store, with manual discrepancy reconciliation. No automatic ledger writes.
organization: Fictional regional apparel retailer; pilot store profile.
business_need: Find size/color stock discrepancies without corrupting the inventory ledger.
users_stakeholders: Store associates, shift leads, Inventory Controller and retail operations sponsor.
adoption_posture: Fast follower; controlled shadow pilots permitted.
capabilities_constraints: Sponsor funds four weeks of one-store shadow counts. Two shift leads passed a count exercise; staff logged a mismatch without penalty. Stockroom has a reader, verified tag-to-SKU list and barcode recount procedure. Inventory Controller approves ledger corrections after recount; scans cannot write to the ledger. One named floor lead plus a trained deputy can collect counts. Both shifts have reserved count time. A signed roster gives the closing lead and deputy queue coverage, recount time and escalation to the controller before any correction. Both shifts completed a handoff drill. No ongoing budget beyond week four.
risk_consequence_context: An unresolved mismatch can produce a wrong availability promise. The manual count remains authoritative.
management_question: Can both shifts operate a four-week shadow pilot now, and can the retailer sustain routine use?
time_horizon: Four-week pilot; reassess before recurring operation.
